subject: Logic
title: What Is a Proof?
description: Learn What Is a Proof? in one minute.

hook.text: A proof isn't persuasion. It's a chain of steps where each follows unavoidably from the last.

buildup.text: In formal logic, a proof starts from axioms or premises and applies inference rules to reach a conclusion.

discovery.text: Every step must be justified by a specific rule: modus ponens, generalization, substitution, and so on.

twist.text: A proof that skips a step is no proof at all. Rigor is what separates demonstration from hand-waving.

climax.text: Proofs make truth mechanical. A computer can check every step without understanding the subject.

quiz.question: What must every step in a formal proof have?
options: A justification by an inference rule
